  "title": "stage_fanout_service discards cleanup_worktree's False, then force-deletes the losing attempt's branch anyway",
  "description": "Filed by lg-external-harness-954's review stage, under that ticket's AC21 (\"filed as follow-up tickets rather than widened into\"). 954 fixed this exact swallow in `worktree_lifecycle`'s three callers and in `reconcile_worktrees`; this was the remaining instance in the tree.\n\n## Original defect\n\n`stage_fanout_service._discard_attempts`, discarding the losing attempts of a fan-out group:\n\n    worktree = session.get(Worktree, attempt.worktree_id) if attempt.worktree_id else None\n    if worktree:\n        service.cleanup_worktree(worktree)\n    if attempt.branch:\n        deleted = run_git([\"branch\", \"-D\", attempt.branch], cwd=repo_root, ...)\n\nThe bool was dropped on the floor and the very next statement force-deleted that attempt's branch. When the removal fails the checkout survives on disk holding commits whose only ref is then deleted with `branch -D`; the attempt's work becomes reachable from nothing but a detached HEAD in a directory no row believes is active. CLAUDE.md, *No silent failures*: a handler must not discard a failure-carrying return.\n\n## State of the tree at this spec (verified by reading it, HEAD 4d0c16a6)\n\n`server/loregarden/services/stage_fanout_service.py:489-513` already carries the fix:\n\n    removal_failed = False\n    if worktree:\n        removal_failed = not service.cleanup_worktree(worktree)\n        if removal_failed:\n            logger.warning(\n                \"Fan-out attempt %s: worktree %s at %s failed to remove; \"\n                \"keeping branch %s instead of force-deleting its only ref\",\n                attempt.id, worktree.id, worktree.worktree_path, attempt.branch,\n            )\n    if attempt.branch and not removal_failed:\n        deleted = run_git([\"branch\", \"-D\", attempt.branch], ...)\n\nThe loop continues to the sibling attempt, and `api/parallel.py:435` is untouched. AC1-AC4 are met by code already in the tree.\n\n## What remains: the pin does not pin\n\n`server/tests/test_stage_fanout_service.py::test_a_losing_branch_survives_a_failed_worktree_removal` passes with the guard deleted. The plan stage ran that mutation (`if attempt.branch and not removal_failed:` \u2192 `if attempt.branch:`) and the test still reported `1 passed`.\n\nThe mechanism: when `cleanup_worktree` is patched to return `False`, `git worktree remove` never ran, so the checkout is still a **registered** worktree. Git refuses `branch -D` on a branch checked out in a registered worktree. Under the mutant the delete *is* attempted, git refuses, and `assert failing_branch in branches` passes anyway. The caplog assertion is also satisfied by the wrong record: the mutant's \"Could not delete discarded fan-out branch <failing_branch>\" message contains the substring it greps for.\n\nSo the end-state assertions measure git's refusal, not the guard. The only observable that distinguishes \"the guard ran\" from \"git saved us\" is the **absence of a `branch -D` invocation** for the failing attempt. AC3's three identifiers (attempt id, worktree row id, path) are currently pinned by nothing.\n\nThe deliverable for this round is a causality oracle for the existing fix \u2014 not a reimplementation of `_discard_attempts`, `cleanup_worktree`, or anything else. Do not re-derive or re-shape the landed guard, its warning text, or its continue-past-failure behaviour.\n\n## Requirement 1166-R1 \u2014 The guard on the losing-attempt discard path is pinned by a causality oracle\n\n### 1. Spec Summary\n\n**Description.** `server/tests/test_stage_fanout_service.py::test_a_losing_branch_survives_a_failed_worktree_removal` is rewritten **in place** (replaced, not supplemented with a second test) so that it fails when the `not removal_failed` guard is removed from `stage_fanout_service._discard_attempts`, and passes on the tree as it stands. It asserts the guard's *cause* \u2014 that no `branch -D` was issued for the attempt whose removal failed \u2014 in addition to the end state it already asserts.\n\n**Constraints.**\n- Production code in `server/loregarden/services/stage_fanout_service.py` is **not** modified by this round. Neither is `server/loregarden/api/parallel.py`.\n- The test is driven through the public entry point `decline_fanout(session, group[\"id\"])`, not the private `_discard_attempts`. `decline_fanout` calls `_discard_attempts(keep_attempt_id=None)` over every attempt with no merge machinery in the way, so it exercises the same path through a real seam.\n- The `run_git` spy must **delegate** to the real `loregarden.services.git_subprocess.run_git` as well as record argv \u2014 the sibling attempt's real `branch -D` and `decline_fanout`'s stage-restore path must still actually run. A spy that returns a canned result is not acceptable.\n- Test isolation uses `unittest.mock` (`patch`/`patch.object`), matching the file's existing style.\n- No new test file, no ticket id in a filename, no report markdown anywhere in the tree.\n\n**Assumptions.**\n- A1: `WorktreeService.cleanup_worktree` returning `False` is a faithful stand-in for a real failed removal at this call site; the existing test's `flaky_cleanup` delegation pattern is kept for the sibling attempt.\n- A2: `_launch(..., count=2)` is the two-attempt fixture to build on, as the current test already does.\n- A3: `loregarden.services.stage_fanout_service.run_git` is the name to patch (module-level import in that service), so patching it does not affect `WorktreeService`'s own git calls.\n\n**Scope / Context.** `server/tests/test_stage_fanout_service.py` only. One test function. No other file in the repository changes under this requirement.\n\n### 2. Acceptance Criteria\n\nSee the ticket's acceptance_criteria list (AC1-AC8). AC1-AC4 are pinning criteria already met by code in the tree and are to be re-verified, not re-implemented; AC5-AC8 are this round's work.\n\n### 3. Risk & Ambiguity Analysis\n\n- **R1 \u2014 A \"branch survived\" assertion is not an oracle for this guard.** Git's refusal to delete a checked-out branch produces the identical end state. Mitigated by AC5(a): assert the absence of the `[\"branch\", \"-D\", failing_branch]` call.\n- **R2 \u2014 A substring caplog assertion matches the wrong record.** Both the guard's warning and the mutant's delete-failure warning name the branch. Mitigated by AC6: assert the three identifiers (attempt id, worktree row id, worktree path), and AC7: assert the delete-failure message does *not* name the failing branch.\n- **R3 \u2014 The sibling's row is gone after the call.** `session.get(Worktree, \u2026)` for the failing attempt must be read **before** the patched call, since the successful sibling's worktree row is deleted by then. Capture attempt ids, the failing attempt's `worktree_id`, and that row's `worktree_path` up front.\n- **R4 \u2014 A non-delegating `run_git` spy makes the test green for the wrong reason.** `decline_fanout` restores the stage map and the sibling delete must really happen; a stubbed `run_git` would leave the sibling branch behind and the second end-state assertion would fail misleadingly. Mitigated by the delegation constraint and AC5(a)'s positive half (the sibling's `branch -D` *is* recorded).\n- **R5 \u2014 Mutation by hand risks losing uncommitted work.** `git checkout --` has destroyed uncommitted work in this repo before. AC8 requires a scripted, reversible swap and a clean-tree proof.\n- **R6 \u2014 Overreach.** The strongest temptation this round is to \"improve\" the landed guard or to widen into sibling tickets lg-external-harness-1165 (`cleanup_worktree` collapses two failure modes into one `False`) and lg-external-harness-1026. Both are separately filed; any finding of that family is a comment on those tickets, not a change here, and not grounds to reject this one.\n\n### 4. Clarifying Questions\n\nNone outstanding. The three that would otherwise block are resolved above by decision: the entry point is `decline_fanout` (not `_discard_attempts`), the oracle is the absent `branch -D` call (not the surviving branch), and the landed production fix is in scope only for re-verification.\n\n### 5. User-facing surfaces\n\n**No user-visible change:** server-side worktree/branch discard path and one backend test. No `client/**` file is touched; no operator-visible surface changes.",
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "AC1 \u2014 `stage_fanout_service._discard_attempts` does not discard `WorktreeService.cleanup_worktree`'s return value at the losing-attempt discard path. Verify by reading `server/loregarden/services/stage_fanout_service.py`: the return is bound (`removal_failed = not service.cleanup_worktree(worktree)`) and read downstream. Met by code already in the tree at 4d0c16a6 \u2014 re-verify, do not re-implement or re-shape.",
    "AC2 \u2014 When the removal fails, the attempt's branch is NOT force-deleted: the `run_git([\"branch\", \"-D\", attempt.branch], \u2026)` call is guarded by `not removal_failed`. Deleting the only ref to commits whose checkout is still on disk is the loss this guard exists to prevent. Met by code already in the tree \u2014 re-verify only.",
    "AC3 \u2014 The failure is observable: on a failed removal, exactly one `logging` record at level `WARNING` or above names the attempt id, the worktree row id, the worktree path, and the branch being kept. Not `debug`/`info`. Met by code already in the tree \u2014 re-verify only; pinned by AC6.",
    "AC4 \u2014 `server/loregarden/api/parallel.py` is NOT changed. Its `cleanup_worktree` call site already raises `HTTPException(400)` on `False` and is correct. Verify with `git diff --name-only` against the merge base: the file must not appear. Do not open it to \"improve\" it.",
    "AC5 \u2014 `server/tests/test_stage_fanout_service.py::test_a_losing_branch_survives_a_failed_worktree_removal` is rewritten in place (replaced, not supplemented) to pin causality, and asserts: (a) **no** recorded `run_git` call has argv `[\"branch\", \"-D\", failing_branch]`, while a recorded call **does** have argv `[\"branch\", \"-D\", ok_branch]`. The test drives the public `decline_fanout(session, group[\"id\"])` over a two-attempt group built with `_launch(..., count=2)`; `WorktreeService.cleanup_worktree` is patched to return `False` only for the failing attempt's branch and to delegate to the real method for the sibling; `loregarden.services.stage_fanout_service.run_git` is wrapped by a spy that records argv **and delegates to the real function**. The failing attempt's id, its `worktree_id`, and that `Worktree` row's `worktree_path` are captured before the patched call (the sibling's row is gone afterwards).",
    "AC6 \u2014 The same test pins AC3 by identifier, not by branch substring: exactly one `caplog` record with `levelno >= logging.WARNING` whose `getMessage()` contains **all three** of `str(failing_attempt_id)`, `str(failing_worktree_id)` and the captured `worktree_path` string.",
    "AC7 \u2014 The same test asserts no emitted record whose message contains \"Could not delete discarded fan-out branch\" names `failing_branch`; such a record appearing means the delete was attempted. It also keeps today's end-state assertions: `failing_branch` still present in `git branch --list`, `ok_branch` absent, and both attempt ids returned in the discard result (the loop must not stop at the first failure).",
    "AC8 \u2014 The new test is proven red under the mutant and green on the unmutated tree, and the proof is attached. Apply the mutant with a scripted, reversible text swap (`if attempt.branch and not removal_failed:` \u2194 `if attempt.branch:`, asserting the expected text is present in each direction) \u2014 never `git checkout --`, which has destroyed uncommitted work in this repo. Required evidence via `loregarden_attach_evidence`: (i) the FAILING run under the mutant, the failure naming assertion AC5(a) and the `[\"branch\", \"-D\", failing_branch]` call, (ii) the PASSING run after revert, (iii) `git status --short` empty after revert, and (iv) `git diff --name-only` showing `server/tests/test_stage_fanout_service.py` as the only changed file. Scope the runs to the tests the change reaches: `uv run pytest tests/test_stage_fanout_service.py -q` (full-suite coverage is CI's job, not this stage's)."

def test_a_losing_branch_survives_a_failed_worktree_removal(session, ticket, repo, caplog):
    """A losing attempt whose worktree removal fails must keep its branch: the
    checkout's commits are reachable from nothing else, so force-deleting the
    branch (`branch -D`) would strand them.

    The oracle is the *absence of the `branch -D` call*, not the surviving
    branch. A failed `cleanup_worktree` leaves the checkout registered with git,
    and git refuses to delete a branch checked out in a registered worktree — so
    "the branch is still there" is satisfied by git's own refusal and passes
    with the guard removed. Only the uninvoked `branch -D` distinguishes the
    guard running from git saving us.

    A sibling attempt whose removal succeeds must still be discarded normally —
    the loop must not stop at the first failure.
    """
    import logging

    from loregarden.services import stage_fanout_service
    from loregarden.services.git_subprocess import run_git as real_run_git
    from loregarden.services.worktree_service import WorktreeService

    group, _ = _launch(session, ticket, count=2)
    failing_attempt_id = group["attempts"][0]["id"]
    ok_attempt_id = group["attempts"][1]["id"]
    failing_branch = group["attempts"][0]["branch"]
    ok_branch = group["attempts"][1]["branch"]

    # Read the failing attempt's worktree row BEFORE the call: the sibling's row
    # is deleted by a successful cleanup, and these identifiers are what the
    # warning must name.
    failing_worktree_id = group["attempts"][0]["worktree_id"]
    failing_worktree_path = session.get(Worktree, failing_worktree_id).worktree_path

    real_cleanup = WorktreeService.cleanup_worktree

    def flaky_cleanup(self, worktree):
        if worktree.branch == failing_branch:
            return False
        return real_cleanup(self, worktree)

    git_calls: list[list[str]] = []

    def spying_run_git(args, **kwargs):
        git_calls.append(list(args))
        return real_run_git(args, **kwargs)

    with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING):
        with (
            patch.object(WorktreeService, "cleanup_worktree", flaky_cleanup),
            patch.object(stage_fanout_service, "run_git", spying_run_git),
        ):
            settled = decline_fanout(session, group["id"])

    # (a) Causality: the guard stopped the force-delete from ever being issued
    # for the attempt whose removal failed, while the sibling's really ran.
    assert ["branch", "-D", failing_branch] not in git_calls, (
        "branch -D was issued for an attempt whose worktree removal failed"
    )
    assert ["branch", "-D", ok_branch] in git_calls, (
        "the sibling attempt's branch must still be force-deleted"
    )

    # (b) The failure is observable, and names the attempt, the worktree row and
    # its path — not just the branch, which the delete-failure warning also
    # names.
    identifying = [
        r
        for r in caplog.records
        if r.levelno >= logging.WARNING
        and str(failing_attempt_id) in r.getMessage()
        and str(failing_worktree_id) in r.getMessage()
        and failing_worktree_path in r.getMessage()
    ]
    assert len(identifying) == 1, (
        "expected exactly one warning naming the attempt, worktree row and path; got "
        f"{[r.getMessage() for r in identifying]}"
    )

    # (c) No delete-failure warning for the failing branch: such a record only
    # exists when the delete was attempted.
    assert not [
        r
        for r in caplog.records
        if "Could not delete discarded fan-out branch" in r.getMessage()
        and failing_branch in r.getMessage()
    ], "the force-delete was attempted and refused, rather than skipped"

    # (d) End state, and the loop did not stop at the first failure.
    branches = git(repo, "branch", "--list").stdout
    assert failing_branch in branches, "branch force-deleted despite a failed removal"
    assert ok_branch not in branches, "the sibling discard must still happen"
    assert set(settled["discarded_attempts"]) == {failing_attempt_id, ok_attempt_id}

Filed by lg-external-harness-1166's review stage (visual_qa lane). **Not grounds to reject 1166** — its AC3 deliberately chose the server log as the observability channel for this failure, and that AC is met. This is the operator-surface half that no AC on 1166 covers.

## What the operator sees

`stage_fanout_service.decline_fanout` (`server/loregarden/services/stage_fanout_service.py`) returns:

    result["discarded_attempts"] = discarded

`_discard_attempts` appends every attempt id to `discarded` whether or not its worktree removal succeeded — correctly, since 1166's AC7 requires the loop to continue past a failure. But the result is the only thing the surface gets. When `cleanup_worktree` returns `False`, the landed guard (4d0c16a6) keeps the branch and logs a `WARNING` naming the attempt, the worktree row and its path, and `decline_fanout` still returns `outcome: declined` with both ids in `discarded_attempts`.

`client/src/components/StageFanoutReview.tsx` renders that: the operator clicks **Keep none** ("Discarding…"), the call returns 200, the group settles, and nothing on screen distinguishes "both worktrees removed" from "one worktree is still on disk and its branch was kept so its commits are not stranded". The operator is the person who would go clean it up, and they are not told it exists.

## The asymmetry

The sibling call site is already honest about this. `server/loregarden/api/parallel.py:435`:

    success = worktree_service.cleanup_worktree(worktree)
    if success:
        return {"status": "cleaned", ...}

— it reports the failure to its HTTP caller. The decline-fanout path reports it only to the log. Same condition, same consequence, two different answers to "does the person find out?". CLAUDE.md, *No silent failures* → *The person using it*: a log line is observable to an operator reading logs, not to the operator who just clicked the button.

## Suggested shape (not settled)

Carry the per-attempt outcome out of `_discard_attempts` rather than a flat id list — e.g. `discarded_attempts` keeping its shape for compatibility plus a `kept_worktrees` list of `{attempt_id, worktree_path, branch}` — and have `StageFanoutReview` render it as a short "1 worktree could not be removed" note with the path, beside the existing `role="alert"` error paragraph.
